artifacts.summary: Verifies Lake's missing -j flag, falsifies LEAN_NUM_THREADS as a concurrency lever via a controlled A/B experiment, confirms flock/systemd-run/PSI availability, and documents lock-derivation, staleness, and self-match-safety recommendations for lake-build-guard.sh.

memory_candidates.content: Lake (Lean build tool) 5.0.0-src has no -j/--jobs flag on `lake build` or `lake`, confirmed by direct invocation (both forms error 'unknown short option -j'). The underlying `lean` binary DOES expose `-j, --threads=num` in `lean --help`, but Lake does not forward any user flag to it -- this is a dead end for a job-count lever via lake build, not a hidden escape hatch.

LEAN_NUM_THREADS does not control Lake's build scheduling/job concurrency: a controlled A/B experiment (same dependency fan-out, only LEAN_NUM_THREADS varied between 1 and 8) on a real Lean project showed identical max concurrent lean-worker descendant count (1) in both trials. A single lean --worker process's own thread count DID vary with the value (Threads: 9 with LEAN_NUM_THREADS=8), consistent with it being an intra-process elaboration thread-pool size, not a job-count lever. Do not ship it as a -j substitute.

Lake's build staleness tracking is content-hash-based, not mtime-based: `touch`ing an already-built Lean source file does not dirty the build or trigger any rebuild. A genuine content edit is required to force a rebuild for testing/experimentation purposes.

`systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryHigh=<v> -p MemoryMax=<v> -- <cmd>` works without root or extra cgroup delegation setup on a standard NixOS/systemd user session, propagates the wrapped command's real exit code correctly, and is composable with command substitution ($(...)) capture patterns.

A Lean project can have long-lived `lean --worker`/`lean --server` LSP elaboration processes coexisting for many hours (observed up to ~11.5 hours) with unrelated `lake build` invocations in the same directory. Any process-based detection of 'is a build in flight' must discriminate build-owned descendants (e.g. via process-tree walk from the launching build's PID) from these ambient editor/LSP workers -- a bare `pgrep lean` or `pgrep -f 'lake build'` will misattribute them.
